title: AnyBlock JSON bundle index
description: One index.json at the root of a bundle describes the bundle as a whole: what the space is called, where a user lands after installing it, and what the sidebar shows. Everything else in a bundle describes a single object; this is the only document that describes the set.

name.description: The space's name, applied on install.

description.description: One line on what the space is for. Author-facing and applied to the space where the client shows one.

iconEmoji.description: The space's icon, as an emoji.

iconImage.description: The space's icon as an image, given as the **name** of an image object shipped in the bundle — not its id. The installer resolves it by querying for an image whose name matches, so the bundle must contain both the image object and its file. A bundle written without image assets should use iconEmoji instead.

entrypoint.description: The object opened once, immediately after the space is created from this bundle — the first thing a user ever sees. Must be an object id from this bundle: a reserved listing cannot be opened.

homepage.description: What opens whenever the user enters the space afterwards. An object id from this bundle; defaults to `entrypoint`. The reserved `widgets` (sidebar dashboard) and `graph` are accepted but are rarely right for a use case — on desktop the widgets are always in the sidebar anyway, so `widgets` wastes the main pane; it only reads well on mobile, which shows one screen at a time. Name a page.

widgets.description: Sidebar widgets, in the order they should appear. Independent of `entrypoint` — declaring one does not require a widget for it. Only give a type a widget when you want fast access to its objects (`layout: "view"`); the sidebar already lists every type automatically, so a link or list widget on a type just duplicates that.

target.description: What the widget points at: an object id from this bundle (a page, a type, a set or a collection), or one of the reserved targets `favorite`, `recent`, `set`, `collection`, `allObjects`, `recentOpen`.

layout.description: How the widget renders. `link` is a single row; `tree` expands children; `list` and `compactList` show contents; `view` renders a type's or set's own view.

limit.description: How many entries a listing widget shows. Ignored by `link`.
